item: CI type-checks src a second time on requirements.lock's own pins (R318, option A)
summary: The test job's mypy run type-checks what -e .[analysis,dev,...] resolves, the newest release of every unbounded dependency, while an install from requirements.lock gets its pins; src/api/diagnostics/keywords.py was red on SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 (the lock) and clean on the 2.1 series CI resolved, and was found a day late (#1576). The lockfile-install job now runs a second mypy over src/ on the lock's own set, and a type error fails that job: five commands, each alone on its line, read the mypy release pyproject's [dev] extra pins into a variable of its own (so a failed read stops the step and the two pins cannot drift), install it, install the lock again with --require-hashes --no-deps to put back anything mypy's install moved, run pip check, then the test job's own mypy command, before the wheel step installs build. Measured with mypy 2.4.1: clean on the lock (761 files, about 22 s), and undoing one of #1576's two lines turns it red on SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 while 2.1.8, what the test job resolved that day (run 42488350732), stays clean. tests/test_ci_mypy_lock_profile.py pins the job's if:, the step, its five commands and their order, the pin source, the step's place and the absence of a default shell, with 31 mutants each named by the checker. lockfile-install is not a required check (making it one is a repository setting). CI/tooling change: no release-notes line.
